To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) students with moderate to severe disabilities can be taught to follow verbal directions, (b) students can be taught to respond to verbal directions that contain multiple components, and (c) students can be trained to respond to verbal instructions that are embedded in a natural context and that are not preceded by a specific training procedure.

1) the use of an instructional program which incorporates the principles and procedures of applied behavior analysis is an effective method for teaching young severely handicapped children to follow verbal directions; 2) the program can be implemented by teachers who have had limited training in behavior modification procedures; and 3) the program can result in a substantial reduction in the time required to teach direction-following skills.
